extension.summary: A Streamlined Utility Tool for Kodi
extension.description: No Bloatware, no Nonsense! Just Keep your Kodi sharp and clean with this utility tool... Now with a Custom Wizard. The "++" fork backs up and restores over Kodi's VFS, so Backup Location / Restore can point straight at a network share (nfs://, smb://) or any VFS path, not just local storage.
extension.news: 2026.07.07.5 - Honest restart prompt: on Fire TV / Android, Kodi cannot restart itself (only desktop Kodi can), so after a restore the prompt now says "Kodi needs to close to finish. Close Kodi now, then reopen it" instead of the misleading "Restart now?". On desktop it still says "Restart". 2026.07.07.4 - Fix: the "wipe clean before restore" step now shows a progress bar ("Wiping the device clean...") instead of a blank, hung-looking gap. On a device with lots of files the wipe can take a while; before, the screen sat empty for up to ~90 seconds between the download finishing and the restore window appearing. It now shows a moving bar the whole time. 2026.07.07.3 - New: Restore now asks "Wipe this device clean before restoring?" - "Yes" makes a clean clone (it removes the current add-ons and settings first, then restores); "No" merges the backup over what is already there. The wipe is SAFE: the chosen backup is staged and validated first, and the box is only wiped once the zip is confirmed good, so a missing or corrupt backup never wipes anything. - IMPORTANT crash fix: restoring a large backup could crash Kodi partway through on Fire TV sticks (the progress screen redrew a changing filename thousands of times and overran the on-screen text renderer). The restore progress no longer shows the per-file name; it shows "Extracting file X of Y" and updates less often, so it no longer crashes, while the bar still moves and always finishes. - Restore now writes your settings (userdata) before add-ons, so if an extract is ever interrupted your irreplaceable settings are already in place and only re-downloadable add-ons would be missing. 2026.07.07.2 - Restore now restores your backup EXACTLY as taken. The previous release re-stamped the backup/restore paths after a restore; that is removed. A restore is a plain extract, and you set the backup location yourself in Settings. 2026.07.07.1 - The add-on's main menu now shows the installed version as a plain line at the bottom (below Settings), e.g. "EZ Maintenance++ 2026.07.07.1". It is read live from the add-on, so it is always accurate. 2026.07.07.0 - IMPORTANT fix (real root cause of the blank Settings screen): Kodi's own Settings dialog for this add-on rendered every label blank because this add-on's settings.xml used plain-text labels and shipped no language file - Kodi resolves settings labels as numeric string ids, so plain text came back empty. This was NOT a Kodi engine bug (a prior release misdiagnosed it as one); a control add-on's Settings dialog renders fine on the same box. Every label now has a proper string id backed by a resources/language strings.po, so the native Settings dialog renders correctly - the standard, supported way. The empty "One-Tap Restore" settings tab is gone (its hidden pin storage moved into Backup/Restore); your stored settings, One-Tap pins, and Dropbox sign-in are unchanged. 2026.07.05.0 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: Kodi's own Settings dialog for this add-on could render completely blank (no categories, no controls, sometimes even the wrong add-on's name in the header) - live-confirmed as a Kodi engine bug, not something fixable in this add-on's settings.xml, reproducing even on a fresh install and on unrelated Kodi-team add-ons. Settings now opens a custom in-app screen instead, covering Backup Location, Restore Location, Destination (Local/Network/Dropbox), keep-count, Dropbox sign-in/keys, and all Maintenance options - reading and writing the exact same settings storage as before, just displayed through a screen that actually works. Backup/Restore also no longer falls back to the broken dialog when the backup location isn't set yet; it opens the same working screen. - The settings.xml schema itself was also migrated to Kodi's modern versioned format (a real, separate defect from the dialog rendering bug above) so the underlying setting values load correctly regardless of which screen displays them. 2026.07.04.6 - The in-app "What's New" display was showing the ENTIRE changelog going back to 2020 (250+ lines) in Kodi's small Add-on Information popup - trimmed to the most recent versions. The full history is unchanged and still lives in this add-on's changelog.txt and in git history; nothing was deleted, only shortened what Kodi displays in that one popup. 2026.07.04.5 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: the 2026.07.04.4 fix wasn't enough - a second real device log showed the fallback copy ALSO failing to read the same local file, proving Kodi's own VFS layer cannot read this backup's freshly-built local zip through any entry point, even though it always correctly reports that file's size. The local file is now read with plain Python file I/O instead of Kodi's VFS for both the copy and its retry, matching how this add-on already builds and validates that same file elsewhere. A remote source (nfs://, smb://) is unaffected and still goes through Kodi's VFS as before. 2026.07.04.4 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: large backup/restore copies to a network share could fail every time with "size mismatch (0 != total)". Root cause found via a real device log: this is a regression from the 2026.07.01.0 progress-bar rewrite, which replaced a plain whole-file copy with a chunked read/write loop so it could show a gauge and support cancel - on some devices (confirmed: tvOS/Apple TV) that chunked reader can come back completely empty on a freshly-built local file even though its size is reported correctly, so no amount of retrying the same chunked copy could ever succeed. The copy now falls back to the original, reliable whole-file copy (itself now also size-verified) whenever the chunked path can't ship the correct number of bytes, instead of giving up. 2026.07.04.3 - Diagnostic only (not a fix): if a backup/restore copy still reports "size mismatch" after the previous release's settle wait, the log now also records how many bytes were actually read and written on that attempt. The previous fix's theory (a large NFS write needing a moment to commit) turned out not to fully explain a real failure still seen after that fix shipped - this pinpoints which side of the copy is actually at fault so the real fix can be targeted correctly instead of guessed again. 2026.07.04.2 - IMPORTANT reliability fix: a large backup/restore copy over NFS could report "size mismatch" and fail even though the write fully succeeded - Kodi's NFS client can take a moment to commit a big write server-side, and checking the size the instant the write closes could catch it too early. The size check now waits briefly for it to settle before giving up, instead of discarding a completed copy and retrying the whole transfer from scratch. 2026.07.04.1 - Fix: backup/restore destination now strips an explicit :2049 port that Kodi's own NFS browse dialog bakes into the path - that form breaks Kodi's NFS write path (VfsCopyError / 0-byte copy). 2026.07.02.0 - Backup/Restore/One-Tap network copies now retry a failed NFS/SMB write instead of giving up on the first try. Kodi's own NFS client can leave a connection stale right after it auto-closes an idle one; a same-instant retry used to hit that same broken connection and fail again, so backups could fail even though the share was fine. Now a failed copy waits a few seconds and tries again (up to 3 attempts total) before reporting failure, giving Kodi room to open a fresh connection. 2026.07.01.1 - IMPORTANT data-loss fix: "Keep how many backups" (rotation) no longer deletes a backup you renamed. It now only prunes the tool's own automatic backups (the ones ending in a date stamp); any backup you renamed, or a "keep" in the name, is protected and never auto-deleted. Renaming a backup used to make it the FIRST one deleted; now it is the safest. Applies to Dropbox and Network/Local. - "Pick a Dropbox backup" is now a live read of the account you are actually signed into. If you switch Dropbox accounts, the list updates to the new account instead of showing the old account's files until the token refreshed. - Menu tidy: the "[ + ]" prefix on empty One-Tap Restore slots is gone.
